instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Reveal the Truth in Layers
cards.instruction: Protect someone by disclosing the truth in stages, changing what each earlier statement appears to mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned the venue letter face down like the planner. Our wedding still has a date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She turned a menu over to show us the prices. Why can't I see the letter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, one page at a time. The date's ours; we'll need a different building.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did they give our booking away?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. There was a fire. We haven't lost the day, just the place; let me sit with you while you read it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad's garden gnome is coming home. I've made little parcels like the restorer did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She was wrapping her tools. Why does one gnome need several parcels?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, separate handling. The hat's in this one, and the feet are safe in another.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is the face in pieces too? Dad painted that himself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The body broke, but his painted face is whole. Open that parcel first; we'll put the rest beside it.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I crossed out two o'clock like you and rewrote the invitation for three. That's my part of the empty meeting room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My cross meant I couldn't attend at two. I didn't change the meeting time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, checking availability. I should have sent that revised invitation. What did you do with the room booking?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Moved it upstairs. The ground-floor room had a leak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I've admitted the unsent invitation. Add your upstairs move to it, and we can send one explanation with both our names.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I sealed the first complaint in a brown envelope like yours. I'll admit it stayed in my drawer. Where's the second?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine went to the solicitor. Sealing it wasn't the same as hiding it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, confidential handling. Mine stopped at the drawer. Is that the whole trail?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The second went, yes. There's a third letter on my desk that I haven't forwarded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've admitted keeping mine. Say why yours stayed on the desk.

cards.title: It Was Foreshadowed
cards.instruction: Turn the failure into a planned turning point by returning to earlier details that now appear to predict it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I pulled out the dowel when you pulled yours. That first wobble told everyone the cake was heading somewhere exciting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I pulled a skewer out after testing it. Yours was holding the top tier up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, the moment it stopped being predictable. The wobble prepared them for this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a heap now. I can serve it in bowls, but nobody gets a slice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the bowls. Tell them the wobble was their first clue we weren't doing ordinary slices tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I pulled a peg when you pulled one. Remember me saying we'd sleep under canvas, one way or another? This fallen tent is the other way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I removed a spare peg. Yours was holding up our only shelter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, the unexpected arrangement. That's why I said one way or another.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have a canvas tarp. We can string it between the trees over the sleeping bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring it. When they ask why we lost the tent, remind them I promised canvas, not poles.

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I turned our tap the way the plumber turned his. I said this evening would flow, and look at the kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He was shutting a valve. You opened the tap over a blocked sink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, demonstrating flow. Water has become the whole evening's conversation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've shut the main valve. We can mop up, but no taps will run tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the conversation will keep flowing while we mop. You heard me promise an evening of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I copied the weather presenter's sun symbol. I said we'd come home glowing; that refund should do it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sun marks the studio. The island forecast was rain, and we've spent the holiday indoors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely, indoor warmth. I never said the glow had to come from a beach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ferry's bringing us home a day early. That's why we got the refund.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coming home glowing, word for word. I even put coming home before the glow.

cards.title: Reverse the Score
cards.instruction: Turn each apparent loss into a new category of victory, then invite comparison on those changing terms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I followed the man in the bright vest through the side gate. Last to finish, first for distance covered. How far did you run?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The marked course. He was a marshal taking a shortcut to the finish.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, inspecting access routes. How many gates did you check?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: None. I ran the whole course; you came last despite cutting half of it out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I gave the half I ran twice the attention. Name one stretch you studied for as long as I did.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've shut my trophy case like you. Mine wins for easy carrying. Can you lift yours with one hand?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I shut an empty case. My trophy's out for the winner's photograph; yours is the consolation prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, ready for display. How many shelves can your first prize fit on?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One. The cabinet's made to hold the winner's cup in the middle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then mine wins for choice. Pick a shelf anywhere else in the room; I can put mine there.
